name: Cordoban arcade
_about: A CORDOBAN ARCADE (the Great Mosque of Cordoba, 785-988): one line of N bays `bay` apart along x, centred, `t` thick along z, standing on the floor. Columns (`order` caliphal) `colH` to the top of the capital, an impost block `impH` on each, the LOWER arch (head `low`: horseshoe in the hall) braced between the imposts, and over the imposts a wall of PIERS `pierW` wide carrying the UPPER arches (head `up`: semicircular) and the gutter at `top`. The heads are words, `low`/`up` + Over and Lobes their numbers: horseshoe, semicircular or lobed. `interlace` yes adds al-Hakam II's interlaced arches, each from a pier to the next but one. The two tiers are what let the hall stand 9.8 m on columns 3 m tall: the lower arch braces, the upper carries (Hernandez Gimenez; Ewert). `ends` 0 leaves out the end columns and piers: a run between two others that already stand on them (or a screen between two arcades).

columns._about: the columns, one under every pier: reused Roman and Visigothic shafts, new caliphal capitals

imposts._about: the impost block on every capital, long along the arcade: the lower arches spring from its ends, the pier stands in its middle

piers._about: the wall over the columns: a pier on every impost, the upper arches between them, the gutter on its top

lower arches._about: the lower arches, braced from impost to impost -- horseshoes in the hall, polylobed in the maqsura

upper arches._about: the upper arches, from pier to pier: the ones that carry

interlaced arches._about: al-Hakam II's interlacing: an arch from every pier to the next but one, so that each crosses its neighbours
